name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,255

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Critical of enclosure fencing developed westward isle

indicators.note: to fence something is to surround it, so the enclosure word goes around the rest
heading west in an across clue means travelling right to left, so the isle is read backwards

blocks.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
fully developed, as fruit is
an ait is a small river island

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of a fence built around an island off to the west.
explanation.walkthrough: PE(RIPE + TIA)N. AIT, a small island in a river such as the Thames, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Peripeteia is the sudden reversal or turning point in a drama, so the adjective describes a crucial, decisive moment.

clue.text: May predecessor out of ingredient for goulash … put in hare!

definitions.note: a whimsical gloss: the animal is classed with the hare

indicators.note: taking one thing out of another removes it

blocks.note: April comes before May, abbreviated
goulash is spiced with paprika

explanation.surface: A cook takes something out of the goulash and puts hare in instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a recipe, but the hare is the zoology: the answer is grouped with hares and rabbits.
explanation.definitionFit: The pika is a small mountain mammal of the order Lagomorpha, the same order as rabbits and their long-eared relatives.

clue.text: An idea used in mechanical procedure for autogiro

indicators.note: something used in another thing is placed inside it

blocks.note: rote is mechanical repetition
a plan is an idea

explanation.surface: An engineer's idea goes into the mechanical procedure for building an early aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: ROT(A PLAN)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotaplane is an aircraft lifted by freely turning rotor blades, the same machine as the early gyroplane design.

clue.text: Edits Philip Roth, mostly changing lover of 11?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
the letters are changed around into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: An editor reworks Philip Roth, who is famous for writing about lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer 11 is PROTHALLI, a stage of the fern life cycle; the question mark flags that the definition goes via that link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pteridophytes are ferns and their relatives, so a pteridophilist is a fern enthusiast, someone fond of plants with prothalli.

clue.text: Melville novel covering second time put into a galley?

indicators.note: a cover goes round what it hides

blocks.note: Typee was Herman Melville's first novel
S is the abbreviation for second
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A sea novel by Melville sets a scene aboard a ship's galley.
explanation.walkthrough: TYPE(S)E + T. The galley is not the ship's kitchen but a printer's tray of set type.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a galley is the tray holding composed type, so text arranged in type for proofing has been put in one.

clue.text: Not sensible to smell a vivid rose when resistance goes up

indicators.note: resistance going means the letter for resistance leaves the word
in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
crimson is a vivid deep red, the colour of a rose

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot smell a bright red rose is told it is fragrant once resistance fades.
explanation.walkthrough: R (the symbol for electrical resistance) leaves CRIMSON, and what remains is reversed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Anosmia is loss of the faculty of smell, so an anosmic person cannot perceive odours at all.

clue.text: Primeval giant with coat of frost returns

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: rimy means covered with rime, a coating of frost

explanation.surface: An ancient giant comes back with frost on him.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: in Norse myth this giant was formed from melting rime ice.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology Ymir is the first being, the frost giant from whose body the world was made.

clue.text: After cycling, tense feeling in the cheeks?

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end to the other

blocks.note: alarm is a tense feeling of fear

explanation.surface: A cyclist ends a ride feeling a tension in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of ALARM moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Malar is an anatomical adjective for the cheekbone or cheek region of the face.

clue.text: Description of monsoon striking north and battling current holding of government land

indicators.note: to strike something out is to remove it, so the letter for north is taken away

blocks.note: a monsoon is rainy weather
abbreviation for north
battling means at war
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A monsoon strikes the north while people fight over government-held land.
explanation.walkthrough: The Anglo-Indian land system fits the monsoon of the surface well.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiyatwari was a system of land tenure in British India in which cultivators held state land directly, paying revenue to government.

clue.text: Revolutionary half of MI6 HQ’s location with great increase in spiky defences

indicators.note: only half the name is kept, the second half being dropped

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
the Secret Intelligence Service building is at Vauxhall Cross in London
def is slang for excellent
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: A spy revolution at MI6 headquarters brings a big boost in barbed defences.
explanation.walkthrough: MI6, Britain's foreign intelligence service, is headquartered at Vauxhall Cross in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheval-de-frise is a timber frame bristling with spikes or blades, used to block cavalry or breach points.

clue.text: Selection of flaky theories to appear up north

indicators.note: a selection is a portion taken out, so a run of letters is lifted from the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, from the end of the first into the second

explanation.surface: Some crackpot theories surface in the north of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up north' marks a Scottish or northern dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Kythe is a Scots verb meaning to show oneself or become visible, a dialect word for emerging.

clue.text: Creator of A Portnoy and everything one supplies sexual generations

blocks.note: Philip Roth wrote Portnoy's Complaint, whose hero is Alexander Portnoy; his name shortens to P Roth
all means everything
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A novelist and all his works seem to churn out a lot of sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Roth's notorious novel is famously about sexual obsession, which makes 'sexual generations' look like literary comment.
explanation.definitionFit: Prothalli are the small plates of tissue in ferns that carry the sex organs: the gametophyte, or sexual, stage of the life cycle.

clue.text: The precise words wife recalled to affirm breadth in light beer

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word for wife comes back in reverse
the pieces before it are placed inside the beer

blocks.note: India pale ale, a light-coloured beer
missis is informal for a wife
to aver is to state firmly
B is the standard abbreviation for breadth

explanation.surface: Over a pale ale, a man insists on exactly what his wife said and how broad things were.
explanation.walkthrough: IP(SISSIM + AVER + B)A. The Latin phrase is spelt out from beer, wife, affirm and breadth.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means 'the very words themselves', used when quoting someone exactly.

clue.text: Supplements come without hard cubes

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for hard is left out

blocks.note: to come about is to happen
H for hard, as on pencils
to cube food is to dice it

explanation.surface: Nutritional supplements arrive minus the hard sugar cubes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cubes' looks like a plural noun, but it is the verb: chops into cubes.
explanation.definitionFit: Appendices are sections added at the end of a book, extra material attached to the main text.

clue.text: Rest after cutting grass’s protective layer of salt

indicators.note: once it has been cut short, the word for rest loses its final letter

blocks.note: peace and quiet is rest
oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: Grass clippings left lying form a protective layer over a salted surface.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. 'Salt' is the old crossword word for a sailor, not sodium chloride.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea coat is the short heavy woollen jacket worn by sailors, a garment protecting an old salt from weather.

clue.text: Rough rule of thumb’s last used in brief calm beset by raucous cry

indicators.note: only the final letter of the thumb is taken
a brief word is cut short, losing its final letter
something used in another thing is put inside it
to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides

blocks.note: the harsh call of a crow
a lull is a period of calm
the final letter of thumb

explanation.surface: A rule of thumb gets drowned out by a noisy shout during a short quiet spell.
explanation.walkthrough: C(LU(B)L)AW. 'Rule of thumb' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'rule'.
explanation.definitionFit: Club-law is government by force or violence, the crude rule of the cudgel instead of any legal order.

clue.text: Grassy land distribution for grazing in the country

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow
sowing is the scattering of seed

explanation.surface: A farmer spreads seed over grassland to provide grazing in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the country' marks a dialect word rather than a rural setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A leasow is a dialect word for pasture, so leasowing is pasturing animals on a meadow.

clue.text: Irishwoman turns to cross quiet battle site

indicators.note: turning round sends the name back the other way
the name lies across the other piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: Maeve is an Irish woman's name, after the legendary queen
the call for quiet

explanation.surface: An Irish woman turns to cross a peaceful battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: EVE(SH)AM. The Worcestershire town gave its name to the 1265 battle in which Simon de Montfort died.
explanation.definitionFit: Evesham, a market town in Worcestershire, England, is where Simon de Montfort was killed in a battle in 1265.

clue.text: Deduct amount from wages to set up aromatic substance producer

indicators.note: in a down clue setting up raises the letters so they read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to dock wages is to deduct from them
a sum is an amount
surface padding that completes the sense of the deducting verb

explanation.surface: An employer docks pay to fund a perfume business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From wages' completes the sense of dock, which is what employers do to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Musk-cod is an old name for a scented thing yielding musk, a perfume used in scenting.

clue.text: FBI raid starts to look likely

indicators.note: a raid that starts up throws things into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An FBI raid starts and seems promising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts' looks like 'beginnings of' and tempts first letters, but here it means jumps about.
explanation.definitionFit: To bid fair is an idiom meaning to seem probable or show promise of something happening.

clue.text: Bachelor that is hosting well-behaved shindy in Edinburgh

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so these letters enclose the next piece

blocks.note: B for bachelor plus IE, the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is
ruly is the rare opposite of unruly

explanation.surface: A single man throws a decorous party in the Scottish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: B(RULY)IE. 'In Edinburgh' marks a Scots word; shindy means a brawl or uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Brulyie is a Scots word for a noisy quarrel or brawl, the same as a commotion or row.

clue.text: Cross old boyfriend: quarrel about name was all over fungus

indicators.note: a quarrel that is about something is wrapped around it
all of the preceding is turned over, so the whole string runs backwards

blocks.note: a cross is the letter X
the standard abbreviation for old
the usual short form of boyfriend
a fuss is a row or quarrel
abbreviation for name
lived means was, existed

explanation.surface: Someone is cross with an old boyfriend after a row about a name that went everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: X O BF FU(N)SS LIVED is assembled first, then the whole string is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil's snuff-box is a folk name for the puffball, a fungus that releases a cloud of dusty spores when squeezed.

clue.text: Rev noisily opposing unoccupied space

blocks.note: V for versus, against
room is free space

explanation.surface: A vicar loudly objects to an empty room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev' looks like a clergyman, but it means gun an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vroom imitates a motor's roar, and as a verb means making an engine growl by accelerating.

clue.text: Vertical bar cut from doughnut-shaped Celtic neck ring

indicators.note: something cut from another is removed from it

blocks.note: a vertical stroke looks like the letter I
toric means shaped like a torus, a ring doughnut

explanation.surface: A bar is cut away from a ring-shaped Celtic necklace.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a rigid twisted metal collar worn by ancient Celts and other Iron Age peoples.

clue.text: What gives a bitter taste in brash films featuring such as …

indicators.note: the first piece is placed inside the word for brash

blocks.note: hops give bitter beer its bitterness
cocky means brash, overconfident

explanation.surface: Something leaves a bitter taste in loud, brash films.
explanation.walkthrough: C(HOPS)OCKY. The clue runs on into 24 across: these are films featuring such as Japanese sword fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-socky is slang for martial-arts action movies, especially kung fu films from Hong Kong.

clue.text: … sword fighting in Japan or India getting one into bother

indicators.note: one thing goes into the other, inside it

blocks.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ado is fuss or bother
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Sword fighting, whether in Japan or India, lands one in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: I + A(I)DO. The clue follows on from 23 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Iai-do is the Japanese martial art of drawing the sword and striking in one smooth motion.

clue.text: Uzbek may spend these years chasing tot

indicators.note: one piece chasing another follows behind it

blocks.note: to tot up is to add, so a tot is a sum
Y is the abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: A man from Uzbekistan might spend years chasing a toddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child, but here it is a sum added up.
explanation.definitionFit: The som is the currency unit of Uzbekistan, and this is its plural form: coins a local would pay with.

clue.text: Even parts of hair receding, badly affected by a certain hormone

indicators.note: even parts are the letters in the second and fourth positions
something done badly comes out wrong, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's hairline is receding badly because of his hormones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receding' tempts a reversal, but it is anagram material along with the even letters of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenergic describes nerves or receptors activated by adrenaline or noradrenaline, the hormones of fight or flight.
